source: KSQAAC Spardha Yashassu NMMS Study Material 2022, MAT Chapter 12 (questions: PDF pages 47-49, solutions: PDF pages 127-128). The pictures are cropped with tools/figures/ch12.json. Every count is worked out by tools/check_counting_figures.ts, which types each figure in as its straight lines and tries every group of corners.

questions.prompt: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Every triangle here has the top corner. Along the base the lines from the top make 4 small parts, and any run of parts next to each other makes a triangle: 1 + 2 + 3 + 4. The short cross line is cut into 3 parts, so it makes 1 + 2 + 3 more.

questions.prompt: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: The lines cut the square into 8 small triangles. Two small ones along one side make a bigger triangle (one on each side), and each diagonal cuts the square into two halves.

questions.prompt: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: The star has a small triangle at each of its 5 points. Each of its 5 lines is also the long side of a bigger triangle: a point together with the part of the middle next to it.

questions.prompt: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: The big triangle has 4 small triangles along each side. Count by size, the ones pointing up and the ones pointing down.
questions.working: Size 1: 10 up + 6 down = 16; size 2: 6 up + 1 down = 7; size 3: 3; size 4: 1; 16 + 7 + 3 + 1 = 27

questions.prompt: How many squares are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: A 4 × 4 grid of squares has 16 small squares, 9 squares of 2 × 2, 4 of 3 × 3 and 1 of 4 × 4.
questions.note: The book prints this grid a little stretched sideways; the small boxes are meant to be squares.

questions.prompt: How many squares are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Count each part of the figure: the 4 squares over the corners, the 4 small squares where they overlap the big square, the big square with its 4 quarters, and the small square in the centre with its 4 quarters.
questions.note: The book prints this figure a little stretched sideways; its boxes are meant to be squares.

questions.prompt: How many squares are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: The square in the middle and its 4 quarters make 5. The tilted square joining the middles of its sides is 1 more, and the 4 tilted squares around it make 4.
questions.note: The book prints this figure a little stretched sideways; its boxes are meant to be squares.

questions.prompt: How many rectangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Count every box whose four sides are all drawn: the whole figure, the strip on the right, everything left of that strip, the strip along the top of it, the part under the top strip, and the two parts that part is cut into.
questions.note: The book's key says A (6 = 4 + 1 + 1), but all 7 of these rectangles have four drawn sides.

questions.prompt: How many rectangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: A rectangle is fixed by 2 of the 5 upright lines and 2 of the 5 cross lines. With 4 boxes in a row there are 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 ways to choose each pair.

questions.prompt: How many rectangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Count every box whose four sides are all drawn, starting with the ones that run from the top to the bottom.
questions.note: Hidden: counting every rectangle whose four sides are drawn gives 22 (10 that run from top to bottom, 2 in the left column, 9 on the right cut by its cross lines, and the small box at the bottom right), which is not an option. The book's key says D, 24.

questions.prompt: How many parallelograms are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Like rectangles in a grid: with 3 parts along a row there are 1 + 2 + 3 ways, and with 2 rows there are 1 + 2 ways. Multiply them.

questions.prompt: How many parallelograms are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: 3 parts along each row and 3 rows: 1 + 2 + 3 ways each way. Multiply them.

questions.prompt: How many pentagons are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: A pentagon has 5 sides. Look for shapes made of the box's sides and the tilted square's sides with exactly 5 corners.
questions.note: Hidden: options A and C are both printed 4, and the key (A) works it out as 3 + 3 + 2 + 2 = 10, which is not 4. It isn't clear which five-sided shapes the book counts.

questions.prompt: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: A box with both diagonals has 8 triangles. Then look for triangles that cross from one box into the next.
questions.note: Hidden: the book's own working gives 29 (8 in each of the 3 boxes, and 5 more that cross from box to box, among them the big one along the long diagonal), and counting every triangle agrees, but 29 is not an option. The key marks B, 6.

questions.prompt: How many triangles are there in the given figure?
questions.rule: Count the triangles in the box, then in the triangle on its right, then the ones that use lines of both.
questions.note: Hidden: the book's 15 (12 in the box and 3 in the triangle on the right) misses two triangles: the middle line runs on to the point, so the centre of the box, a right-hand corner of the box and the point make a triangle, at the top and at the bottom. That gives 17, which is not an option.
